specific_title: City of Thibodaux HRC Prop#1 -- HRC Amend. - CC- Mayor
summary_text: City of Thibodaux Home Rule Charter Amendment Propositions  Proposition No. 1  Summary:  Amendment to Article III, Section 3(B) of the current home rule charter of the City of Thibodaux, State of Louisiana, as it pertains to Qualifications of a Candidate for Election as Mayor.
full_text: Shall Article III, Section 3B of the City Charter of the City of Thibodaux be amended to read as follows:   "Article III - Organization, Structure and Distribution of Powers and Functions Section 3. The Executive Branch B. Qualifications of a Candidate for Election as Mayor (1) To qualify as a candidate for the Office of Mayor, the prospective candidate shall have resided in, and been a qualified elector in, the City for at least one year prior to the end of the period for qualifying as a candidate for that position. (2) A candidate for election as Mayor shall not qualify as a candidate for any other elected public office. (3) The Mayor shall be elected according to the election laws of the State of Louisiana for a four (4) year term concurrent with that of the Council and shall be eligible for re-election; but no person, including the Mayor in Office at the time of the adoption of this amended Section, shall be eligible as a candidate for election or re-election to the Office of Mayor for the term immediately following the third consecutive term to which that person was elected as Mayor. (4) A candidate for Mayor shall be elected when he/she receives a majority of the votes of the electors in an election for Mayor"?

specific_title: City of Thibodaux HRC Prop#2 -- HRC Amend. - CC - Exec. Branch
summary_text: City of Thibodaux Home Rule Charter Amendment Propositions  Proposition No. 2  Summary:  Amendment to Article III, Section 3(E) of the current home rule charter of the City of Thibodaux, State of Louisiana, as it pertains to Departments, Offices, Boards, Commissions and Agencies.
full_text: Shall Article III, Section 3E of the City Charter of the City of Thibodaux be amended to read as follows: "Article III - Organization, Structure and Distribution of Powers and Functions  Section 3. The Executive Branch E. Departments, Offices, Boards, Commissions and Agencies (7) Within sixty days after assuming office, a newly elected Mayor shall submit his/her nominations for the heads of all departments, except Civil Service, to the Council for confirmation. A re-elected Mayor shall be required to submit existing department heads under his/her supervision to the Council for reconfirmation. Within thirty days thereafter, the Council shall vote to either confirm or reject each nomination. If a nomination for head of a department is confirmed by the Council, the person confirmed shall assume the office and serve thereafter at the pleasure of the Mayor. If a nomination for head of a department is rejected by the Council, the person rejected shall not assume the office to which nominated, and the Mayor shall submit a new nomination within sixty days after the date of the rejection. The person rejected shall not be eligible for renomination for the position involved for a period of six months after the date of the rejection vote. The Mayor may appoint an interim department head who shall serve until a permanent department head is confirmed. If a vacancy occurs in the office of any department head after a person has been initially confirmed in that position, the Mayor shall submit a nomination to fill the vacancy to the Council within sixty days after the date on which the vacancy occurs. The Council shall act on the nomination within thirty days thereafter"?

specific_title: Sunday Alcohol Sales -- Sunday Sales - PC
summary_text: Sunday Alcohol Sales Proposition  Summary:  Requiring the Parish Council of the Parish of West Baton Rouge to amend Chapter 6, Section 23(2) and Chapter 6, Section 116(2) of the Compiled Ordinances of the Parish of West Baton Rouge, for the purpose of prohibiting the sale of all alcoholic beverages and the closure of the business selling alcoholic beverages on Sundays at 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m. on Monday, provided that the 10:00 p.m. Sunday closing time shall not apply to Super Bowl Sundays, a Sunday which is followed by either Memorial Day, Labor Day, the 4th of July or New Year's Day, or if the Sunday is the 4th of July, and providing that restaurants, grocery stores, drugstores, off-track betting parlors and truck stop casinos may remain open and may sell alcoholic beverages and/or permit the consumption of alcoholic beverages in such place of business during the prohibited periods set forth above.
full_text: Shall the Parish Council of the Parish of West Baton Rouge be required to amend Chapter 6, Section 23(2) and Chapter 6, Section 116(2) of the Compiled Ordinances of the Parish of West Baton Rouge to provide that the sale of all alcoholic beverages must stop and the business selling such alcoholic beverages shall be closed on Sundays at 10:00 p.m. and may not reopen until 6:00 a.m. on Monday, provided that the 10:00 p.m. Sunday closing time shall not apply to Super Bowl Sundays, a Sunday which is followed by either Memorial Day, Labor Day, the 4th of July or New Year's Day, or if the Sunday is the 4th of July, and further providing that restaurants, grocery stores, drugstores, off-track betting parlors and truck stop casinos may remain open and may sell alcoholic beverages and/or permit the consumption of alcoholic beverages in such place of business during the prohibited periods set forth above?

full_text: Shall the Mayor and the City Council of the City of Port Allen be required to amend the Code of Ordinances of the City of Port Allen to provide that the sale of all alcoholic beverages must stop and the business selling such alcoholic beverages shall be closed on Sundays at 10:00 p.m. and may not reopen until 6:00 am. on Monday, provided that the 10:00 p.m. Sunday closing time shall not apply to Super Bowl Sundays, a Sunday which is followed by either Memorial Day, Labor Day, the 4th of July or New Year's Day, or if the Sunday is the 4th of July, and further providing that restaurants, grocery stores, drugstores, off-track betting parlors, if any, and truck stop casinos, if any, may remain open and may sell alcoholic beverages and/or permit the consumption of alcoholic beverages in such place of business during the prohibited periods set forth above?

specific_title: PW School Board -- 6.08 Mills - SB - 5 Yrs.

R.S. 47:301 to 317, inclusive (the "Tax"), with the avails of the Tax (after paying reasonable costs of collecting and administering the Tax) dedicated and used for the purposes of constructing, acquiring, operating, maintaining, or improving Public Safety, Fire Protection, and criminal justice facilities, operations, and equipment, and other operating expenses of the City; and, authorization to fund avails of the Tax into bonds in various series at various times, to be used to fund capital costs of the City, including the purchase of Fire Trucks or other public safety equipment, as permitted by Louisiana law, including Sub-Part F, Part III, Chapter 4, Title 39 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950, as amended, said Tax to be levied in lieu of an existing tax of the same amount approved by the voters on April 6, 2002, the levy of which shall then be permanently terminated and cancelled?

specific_title: Village of Pine Prairie -- 2% S&U - Mayor & BOA

full_text: Shall Jefferson Parish exempt from ad valorem taxation the next seven thousand five hundred dollars of the assessed valuation after the homestead exemption of property receiving the homestead exemption which is owned and occupied by a veteran with a service-connected disability rating of one hundred percent as determined by the United States Department of Veterans Affairs; and shall the surviving spouse of a veteran be eligible for this exemption if this exemption was in effect on the property prior to death of the veteran, all in accordance with the provisions of Article VII, Section 21(K) of the Constitution of Louisiana, said exemption to extend and apply in Jefferson Parish and become effective only after the question of its adoption has been approved by a majority of the registered voters of the Parish voting in an election held for that purpose?

specific_title: PW HRCAmd.Art.IVSec.4-06(b)&(c) -- PC-Art. IV, Sec. 4-06(b) & (c)
summary_text: Parishwide Proposition (Charter Amendment) (Section 4-06 (b) and (c))  Summary:  Amendment to Article IV, to amend Section 4-06 (b) and (c) of the St. Bernard Parish Home Rule Charter to change the qualifications of the director of community development and also change the duties of said department.
full_text: Shall Article IV, Section 4-06 (b) and (c) of the Home Rule Charter of the Parish of St. Bernard, State of Louisiana, be amended to read as follows: (b) The director of community development at the time of appointment shall have at least a master's degree in land use planning, public administration, or a related field from an accredited college or university with a minimum of two (2) years experience in the areas of zoning and subdivision review, building inspection and permits. (c) The director of community development shall direct and be responsible for the following activities: (1) Maintenance of maps related to the functions of the department; (2) Coordination of planning activities; (3) Provide support staff for the planning commission and board of zoning adjustments; (4) Inspection, licensing, and permit issuance in conjunction with the enforcement of any zoning ordinances and building, housing, and other technical codes; (5) Issuance of permits for mineral exploration and seismic activity; (6) Issuance of oil and gas permits; (7) Act as the flood plain manager; (8) Facilitate referrals for resolution and monitor environmental concern issues; (9) Serve as the secretary of the Planning Commission and the Board of Zoning Adjustments; (10) Other such activities within the scope of this office as may be directed by the president?

specific_title: PW HRCAmd.Art.IVSec.4-09 -- PC-Art. IV, Sec. 4-09

full_text: Shall Article IV, Section 4-09 of the Home Rule Charter of the Parish of St. Bernard, State of Louisiana, be amended to read as follows:   Sec. 4-09. Department of human resources.  (a)  The head of the department of human resources shall be the St. Bernard Parish Director of Human Resources (hereinafter referred to as the director of human resources). (b)  The director of human resources at the time of appointment shall have a bachelor's degree in human resources, public administration, business administration, or a related field from an accredited college or university with a minimum of two (2) years experience in human resources management and benefits administration in government service or in the private sector supervising an employee base of fifty percent (50%) the size of St. Bernard Parish Government?

specific_title: City of Hammond HRC Am.- 5 -- Police Chief Qualifications - CC
summary_text: City of Hammond Charter Amendment Propositions Charter Amendment Proposition No. 5 (Police Chief Qualifications)  Summary:  Amendment to Article IV, Section 4-04 of the Home Rule Charter to add a Subsection C to provide for the qualifications of the police chief.
full_text: Shall Article IV, Section 4-04 of the Home Rule Charter for the City of Hammond be amended to add a Subsection C to read as follows: C. The police chief must meet all requirements of the municipal fire and police civil service laws of the State of Louisiana as applicable to the City of Hammond, including being a citizen of the United States. The police chief candidate must meet one of the following qualifications:  (1) Must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution of higher education in criminal justice, police administration, public administration, or other related curriculum and at least six (6) years experience of progressively responsible positions in law enforcement, at least two (2) years of which must have been in positions which include administrative or supervisory responsibilities. Law enforcement experience should include work in positions which would provide background in patrol operations, criminal investigations, police training, and related areas of police department operations and management, or; (2) Must have an associate degree from an accredited institution of higher education in criminal justice, police administration, or other related curriculum, or a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution of higher education in an unrelated curriculum and at least eight (8) years experience of progressively responsible positions in law enforcement, at least two (2) years of which must have been in positions which include administrative or supervisory responsibilities. Law enforcement experience should include work in positions which would provide background in patrol operations, criminal investigations, police training, and related areas of police department operations and management.

specific_title: City of Hammond HRC Am.- 6 -- Fire Chief Qualifications - CC
summary_text: City of Hammond Charter Amendment Propositions Charter Amendment Proposition No. 6 (Fire Chief Qualifications)  Summary:  Amendment to Article IV, Section 4-05 of the Home Rule Charter to add a Subsection C to provide for the qualifications of the fire chief.
full_text: Shall Article IV, Section 4-05 of the Home Rule Charter for the City of Hammond be amended to add a Subsection C to read as follows: C. The fire chief must meet all requirements of the municipal fire and police civil service laws of the State of Louisiana as applicable to the City of Hammond, including being a citizen of the United States. The fire chief candidate must meet one of the following qualifications:  (1) Must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution of higher education in fire science, fire administration, public administration, or other related curriculum and at least six (6) years experience of progressively responsible positions in fire service, at least two (2) years of which must have been in positions which include administrative or supervisory responsibilities. Fire service experience should include work in positions which would provide background in fire prevention and investigation, fire training, and related areas of fire department operations and management, or; (2) Must have an associate degree from an accredited institution of higher education in fire science, fire administration, or other related curriculum, or a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution of higher education in an unrelated curriculum and at least eight (8) years experience of progressively responsible positions in fire service, at least two (2) years of which must have been in positions which include administrative or supervisory responsibilities. Fire service experience should include work in positions which would provide background in fire prevention and investigation, fire training, and related areas of fire department operations and management.

specific_title: City of Hammond HRC Am.- 7 -- Conflicts of Interest - CC
summary_text: City of Hammond Charter Amendment Propositions Charter Amendment Proposition No. 7 (Conflicts of Interest)  Summary:  Amendment to Article VII, Section 7-02 of the Home Rule Charter to expand the prohibition against conflicts of interests to include interests in limited liability corporations and partnerships.
full_text: Shall Article VII, Section 7-02 of the Home Rule Charter for the City of Hammond be amended to read as follows: Section 7-02.  Conflict of Interest Any City officer, official or employee who has a substantial financial interest, direct or indirect or by reason of ownership of interest in any limited liability company, partnership, or any other business corporation, in any contract with the City or in the sale of any land, material, supplies or services to the City or to a contractor or subcontractor supplying the City shall make known that interest and shall be prohibited from voting or otherwise participating in the capacity of a City officer or employee in the making of such sale or in the making or performance of such contract. Any City officer, official or employee who willfully conceals such a substantial financial interest or willfully violates the requirements of this section shall be guilty of malfeasance in office or position and shall forfeit the office or position. Violation of this section with the knowledge, express or implied of the person, partnership, company or corporation contracting with or making a sale to the City shall render the contract or sale void.

specific_title: City of Hammond HRC Am.- 8 -- Amendment/Replacement
summary_text: City of Hammond Charter Amendment Propositions Charter Amendment Proposition No. 8 (Amendment or Replacement)  Summary:  Amendment to Article VII, Section 7-04 of the Home Rule Charter to change the word "repeal" to the word "replace".
full_text: Shall Article VII, Section 7-04 of the Home Rule Charter for the City of Hammond be amended to read as follows: Section 7-04. Amending or replacing the charter A. Proposals to amend or replace this charter may be made both by the council and by petition signed by not less than twenty-five (25) percent of the qualified voters of the City. The procedures and time limits for filing such a petition, for holding a public hearing on the matter and for calling an election on the petition request shall be the same as provided for in Section 6-01 (Initiative and Referendum).  A petition shall contain the full text of the proposed amendment.  B. Proposals to amend or replace this charter shall be submitted for ratification to the qualified voters of the City, preferably in an election already scheduled for other purposes, otherwise in a special election called by the council. The results shall be determined by a majority vote of the electors voting on any particular proposal.  C. Proposals by the council and by petition may be submitted to the voters at the same election and voters may, at their option, accept or reject any or all such proposals. Should conflicting proposals be approved at the same election, the one receiving the greater number of affirmative votes shall prevail to the extent of such conflict.  D. Proposals to amend or replace this charter shall not be submitted more often than every two (2) years and no amendment or replace shall shorten the term for which any official was elected or reduce the salary of office for that term.

full_text: Shall the Parish of Beauregard, State of Louisiana (the "Parish"), under the provisions of Article VI, Section 29 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974, and other constitutional and statutory authority, be authorized to levy and collect a tax of one-fourth of one percent (1/4%) (the "Tax") upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption, and the storage for use or consumption, of tangible personal property and on sales of services in the Parish, all as defined by law (an estimated $1,207,917 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the Tax for an entire year), for a period of fifteen (15) years, from and after January 1, 2013, with the proceeds of the Tax (after paying the reasonable and necessary expenses of collecting and administering the Tax), to be dedicated and used for the purpose of constructing, expanding, improving, renovating, operating and maintaining the Beauregard Parish Courthouse (the "Courthouse"), including acquiring equipment, fixtures and furnishings therefor, with the proceeds of the Tax being subject to funding into bonds for constructing, expanding, improving and renovating the Courthouse, including acquiring equipment, fixtures and furnishings therefor, to the extent and in the manner permitted by the laws of Louisiana?

specific_title: Town of Arcadia (Const.& Str.) -- 1% S&U - TC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Town of Arcadia Propositions (1% Sales Tax)   Summary:  Authority to (i) enact a previously enacted one percent (1%) sales and use tax authorized to be levied by the Town of Arcadia through June 31st, 2012, pursuant to an election held originally on May 2, 1987, as follows:  (a) 30% for construction, paving, resurfacing, improving, and/or maintaining public streets in the Town, (b) 10% for acquiring, maintaining, improving, and supporting parks and recreation programs in and for the Town, including facilities and equipment therefore, (c) 10% for industrial construction, inducement, and/or procurement, including purchasing land for an industrial park, and (d) 50% for general operating revenue for the Town, and (ii) levy and collect the tax for an additional ten (10) years from and after January 1st, 2013, with the proceeds of the tax subject to funding into bonds.
full_text: Shall the Town of Arcadia, State of Louisiana, (the "Town"), under the provisions of Article VI, Section 29 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974 and other constitutional and statutory authority (i) be authorized to levy a One Percent (1%) sales and use tax previously authorized to be levied by the Town through June 1, 2012, pursuant to an election originally held on May 2, 1987 and which had been previously continued but which inadvertently lapsed in June, 2012, (the "Tax") as follows:  (a) 30% for constructing, paving, resurfacing, and/or maintaining public streets in the Town; (b) 10% for acquiring, maintaining, improving, and supporting parks and recreation programs in and for the Town, including facilities and equipment therefore; (c) 10% for industrial construction, inducement, and/or procurement, including purchasing land for an industrial park; and (d) 50% for general operating revenue for the Town; and (ii) shall the Town be further authorized to levy and collect the Tax for an additional Ten (10) years from and after January 1st, 2013, with the proceeds of the Tax being subject to funding into bonds to be issued for any of the capital purposes set forth above in the manner permitted by the laws of Louisiana including Sub-Part F, Part III, Chapter 4, Title 39 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950 as amended; with the proceeds of said tax being estimated to be Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars annually, conditioned upon the taxable sales within the Town of Arcadia?

specific_title: Town of Arcadia(Rds,Bridg.Drain) -- .50% - TC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Town of Arcadia Propositions (0.50% Sales Tax)  Summary:  Authority to levy a one half percent (0.50%) sales and use tax for additional solid waste collection and disposal not provided by the Bienville Parish Police Jury and for public roads, bridges and drainage in the Town of Arcadia.
full_text: Shall the Town of Arcadia, State of Louisiana, (The "Town") under the provisions of Article VI, Section 29 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974, and other constitutional and statutory authority, be authorized to levy and collect, and adopt an ordinance providing for such levy and collection, a tax of One-Half Percent (0.50%) (the "Tax") upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption and the storage for use or consumption, of tangible personal property and on sales of services in the Town, as defined in La. R.S. 47:301 through 47:317, for a period of Ten (10) years from and after January 1st, 2013 (Effective Date), with the avails or proceeds of the Tax (after paying the reasonable and necessary expenses of collecting and administering the Tax) to be dedicated and used as follows:  First:  To provide for the building, constructing, improving, and maintaining of public roads and drainage facilities in the Town (but no proceeds will be used for salaries); and Second:  To provide for the supplemental collection and disposal of solid waste within and for the Town which is not currently being collected by other governmental agencies, including the payment of contracts providing therefore and acquiring, constructing, improving, maintaining and operating equipment and facilities necessary therefore (but no proceeds will be used for salaries); with the proceeds of the tax being estimated to be Three Hundred and Fifty Thousand Dollars annually, conditioned upon the taxable sales within the Town of Arcadia?

full_text: Shall Melrose East Crime Prevention District ("District") be authorized to levy an annual parcel fee of up to two hundred dollars ($200) per improved residential parcel and an initial parcel fee of up to five hundred dollars ($500) per improved commercial parcel located in the District for a period of ten (10) years, beginning in 2013 and ending in 2022, to aid in crime prevention and to add to the security of District residents by increasing the presence of law enforcement personnel in the District and for all purposes set forth in La. full_text: Shall the Zachary Community School System, in the Parish of East Baton Rouge, State of Louisiana (the "System"), continue to levy a thirty-eight and two-tenths (38.2) mills tax on all property subject to taxation in said System for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2014 and ending with the year 2023 (an estimated $7,500,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), inclusive, for the purpose of giving additional support to the public elementary and secondary schools of the Zachary Community School System and for any of its lawful school purposes, including acquiring, constructing, improving, maintaining and operating the public elementary and secondary schools and school-related buildings, equipment and facilities of the System and paying the salaries and benefits of school system personnel?

specific_title: MayfairPark/MPEast/MHeightsCrimeImpD -- $144 Parcel Fee - BOC - 5 Yrs.
summary_text: Mayfair Park/Mayfair Park East/Mayfair Heights Crime Prevention Improvement District Proposition  Summary:  Authorization for the Mayfair Park/Mayfair Park East/Mayfair Heights Crime Prevention Improvement District to levy an annual parcel fee of $144 for each parcel of improved land located in the boundaries of the district for a period of five (5) years commencing on January 1, 2013, owned by a person under the age of sixty-five at the time of voter approval; to be used to aid in crime prevention and enhance security of district residents by providing for an increase of law enforcement personnel or contracted security personnel in the district and other purposes permitted by applicable law within the Mayfair Park/Mayfair Park East/Mayfair Heights Crime Prevention Improvement District.
full_text: Shall Mayfair Park/Mayfair Park East/Mayfair Heights Crime Prevention Improvement District, acting through the Board of Commissioners of the District be authorized to levy an annual parcel fee of One Hundred Forty-Four Dollars ($144.00) on each improved parcel located within the boundaries of the District, less and except any parcel whose owner is sixty-five or older at the time of voter approval, for a period of five (5) years, beginning in 2013 and ending in 2017 (an estimated $61,871 is reasonably expected to be collected from the initial levy), which fee shall be collected by any means authorized by law for the collection of taxes, all as provided by La. R.S. 33:9097.13, with the proceeds of said fee (after deducting the reasonable and necessary costs of collecting said fee) to be used to aid in crime prevention and enhance security of District residents by providing for an increase of law enforcement personnel or contracted security personnel in the District and for other purposes permitted by applicable law. Provides that it is the purpose and intent that the additional law enforcement personnel and their services provided through the fee shall be supplemental to and not in lieu of personnel and services provided in the district by the city and parish.  Provides that if the district ceases to exist, district funds shall be transmitted to the governing authority of East Baton Rouge Parish and requires that such funds be used for law enforcement purposes in the area included within the district.

summary_text: Parishwide Proposition  (Sales Tax Renewal)  Summary:  Authority to renew a 1/4% sales tax for 10 years with the proceeds to be used as follows:  (1) to pay the cost of maintaining and operating a Parishwide mosquito control program, including the cost of acquiring land, buildings and equipment necessary in connection therewith; and (2) the balance of the proceeds to be divided annually on or before May 1st of each year, between the Parish and the incorporated municipalities of the parish on a per capita basis according to the 2010 U.S. Census, for the purpose of constructing, acquiring and improving drainage facilities; with authority to fund their respective proceeds into bonds for paying the cost of the aforesaid capital improvements.
full_text: Shall the Parish of Iberia, State of Louisiana (the "Parish"), under the provisions of Article VI, Section 29 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974, and other constitutional and statutory authority supplemental thereto, be authorized to continue to levy and collect a tax of one-fourth of one percent (1/4%) (the "Tax") upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption and storage for use or consumption of tangible personal property and on sales of services in the Parish, all as defined by law (an estimated $3,250,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the Tax for an entire year), for a period of ten (10) years, from and after August 1, 2013, with the proceeds of the Tax (after paying the costs of collecting and administering the Tax), to be used as follows:  (1) To pay the cost of maintaining and operating a Parishwide mosquito control program, including the cost of acquiring land, buildings and equipment necessary therefor; and (2) The balance of the proceeds to be divided annually on or before May 1st of each year, between the Parish and the incorporated municipalities of the Parish on a per capita basis according to the 2010 U.S. Census, for the purpose of constructing, acquiring and improving drainage facilities; and further, shall the Parish and the municipalities in the Parish be authorized to fund their respective proceeds of the Tax into bonds to pay the cost of the aforesaid capital improvements to the extent and in the manner permitted by the laws of Louisiana, including Sub-Part F, Part III, Chapter 4, Title 39 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950, as amended?

summary_text: City of Jennings Proposition (Sales Tax)  Summary:  25-year 1% sales and use tax ("Tax") beginning January 1, 2013, with collections from the tax estimated to be $2,400,000.00 for one year, for acquiring, constructing, improving, operating and maintaining streets, garbage, parks, fire and police departments, public buildings, drainage, heavy equipment purchases, jail operations, police pension payments, economic development activities, sewage collection and disposal facilities, and waterworks facilities, including payment of any bonded or funded indebtedness incurred for such purposes, and including salaries of employees for any one or more of said purposes, in lieu of the 1% sales and use tax approved July 16, 1994, rededicated November 15, 1997.
full_text: Shall the City of Jennings, Louisiana (the "City"), be authorized to levy and collect for a period of twenty-five years beginning January 1, 2013, a tax of one percent (1%) upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption and storage for use or consumption of tangible personal property and on sales of services in the City, all presently or hereafter defined in La. R.S. 47:301 through La. R.S. 47:317 (the "Tax"), in lieu of the 1% sales and use tax approved July 16, 1994, rededicated November 15, 1997, with collections from the levy of the Tax estimated to be $2,400,000.00 for one year, for the following purposes and in the priorities hereinafter set forth: 1. At least $500,000 annually to pay any bonded or funded indebtedness of the City incurred for sewage collection and disposal facilities; and  2. The remaining proceeds of the Tax to be used for acquiring, constructing, improving, operating and maintaining streets, garbage, parks, fire and police departments, public buildings, drainage, heavy equipment purchases, jail operations, police pension payments, economic development purposes and activities, sewage collection and disposal facilities, and the city's waterworks facilities, including payment of any bonded or funded indebtedness of the city incurred for such purposes, and including salaries of city employees for any one or more of said purposes; and further shall the City be authorized to fund the proceeds of the Tax into bonds to pay the cost of capital improvements for the aforesaid purposes to the extent and in the manner permitted by the laws of Louisiana, including Sub-Part F, Part III, Chapter 4, Title 39 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950, as amended?

full_text: Shall the School District Number A (Parishwide) of the Parish of Morehouse, State of Louisiana, incur debt and issue bonds not exceeding Two Million Six Hundred Sixty-Five Thousand Dollars ($2,665,000), to run not exceeding twenty (20) years from date thereof, with interest at a rate not exceeding eight per centum (8%) per annum, for the purpose of acquiring and/or improving lands for building sites and playgrounds; including construction of necessary sidewalks and streets adjacent thereto; purchasing, erecting and/or improving school buildings and other school related facilities within and for the District and acquiring the necessary equipment and furnishings therefore, title to which shall be in the public; which bonds will be general obligations of the District and will be payable from ad valorem taxes to be levied and collected in the manner provided by Article VI, Section 33 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974 and statutory authority supplemental thereto, with no increase in the estimated millage rate to be levied in the first year of issue above the 10 mills currently being levied to pay General Obligation Bonds of the District?

specific_title: PW Communication Dist. -- 911 Service Charge - CC
summary_text: Parishwide Proposition (Communication District)  Summary: Establish/Increase the fixed rate emergency telephone service charge for 9-1-1 services for all Orleans Parish residential and commercial service users, wireless commercial mobile radio service connections, and residential and commercial interconnected voice over internet protocol service access line equivalents, to be levied in perpetuity.

full_text: Shall the Law Enforcement District of the Parish of Winn, State of Louisiana (the "District"), be authorized to levy and collect a tax of one-half of one percent (1/2%) (the "Tax"), (an estimated $900,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), in perpetuity, from and after January 1, 2014, upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption, and storage for use or consumption, of tangible personal property and on sales of services in the District, with the proceeds of the Tax (after paying the reasonable and necessary costs and expenses of collecting and administering the Tax) to be dedicated and used for the purpose of providing additional support for the Winn Parish Sheriff's Department (the "Department"), including but not limited to, acquiring, improving, maintaining and operating law enforcement facilities, vehicles and equipment and funding general operations of the Department?

specific_title: Tamaron Subdivision Improv. Dist. -- Parcel Fee 250 - CC - 8 Yrs.
summary_text: Tamaron Subdivision Improvement District Proposition
full_text: Shall the city of New Orleans levy a special annual fee (except that no fee shall be imposed upon any parcel whose owner qualified for the special assessment level provided by Article VII, Section 18(G)(1) of the Louisiana Constitution), to be called the Tamaron Subdivision Improvement District Fee, on each parcel of land in the Tamaron Subdivision Improvement District (which district is comprised of that area of the city of New Orleans located within the following boundaries: North I-10 Service Road, Morrison Road, Kingswood Subdivision and Gannon Road) in an amount not to exceed two hundred fifty dollars ($250) for eight (8) years, commencing on January 1, 2015 and ending December 31, 2022, which fee is estimated to generate approximately twenty two thousand dollars ($22,000) annually, to be used solely and exclusively to promote and encourage the security, beautification and overall betterment of the Tamaron Subdivision Improvement District as determined and managed by the Board of Commissioners of the Tamaron Subdivision Improvement District, which additional security (public or private) provided by the district shall be supplemental to and not in lieu of personnel and services provided in the district by the New Orleans Police Department?

specific_title: Lake Bullard Neighbor. Imp. Dist. -- Parcel Fee 250 - CC - 4 Yrs.

specific_title: Hurstville Sec. & Neigh. Imp. Dist. -- Parcel Fee 550 plus 25  -  CC - 8 Yrs.

specific_title: Mid-City Security District -- Parcel Fee 200-250 or 300-375-CC-5 Yrs.
summary_text: Mid-City Security District Proposition

specific_title: PW HRC Amendment Sec. 3 -- CC - Sec. 3-102 & 4-201
summary_text: Parishwide Proposition (City Charter Amendment) (Inauguration Dates for Mayor and Council)
full_text: Shall City Charter Sections 3-102 and 4-201 be amended, effective June 1, 2018, to read as follows:  Section 3-102. Number and Terms of Councilmembers.  The Council shall consist of seven members, of whom five shall be elected from districts, one from the City at-Large as Councilmember-at-Large, Division "1" and one from the City at-Large as Councilmember-at-Large, Division "2", each to be voted on as separate offices. The terms of councilmembers shall be four years beginning the second Monday in January next following their election except that a councilmember elected to fill a vacancy shall serve only for the remainder of the unexpired term.  The two Councilmember-at-Large offices shall not be considered to be new or different offices for purposes of Section 3-105(3) herein.  Section 4-201. Election and Term. The electors of the City shall elect a Mayor at an election to be held in accordance with the election laws of the State. The Mayor shall take office on the second Monday in January and every four years thereafter following election. A person who has served as Mayor for more than one and one-half terms in two consecutive terms shall not be eligible for election as Mayor for the succeeding term?

specific_title: PW HRC Amendment Prop. No. 3 -- Sec. 3-07(B) - PC
summary_text: Parishwide Home Rule Charter Amendment Propositions Proposition No. 3
full_text: Shall Section 3-07(B) of the Iberia Parish Home Rule Charter be amended to read as follows: "Section 3-07. Vacancies. B. A vacancy in the office of President shall be filled by appointment of a person meeting the qualifications for office by a majority of the authorized membership of the Council. If eighteen (18) months or less of the unexpired term remains when the vacancy occurs, the appointment shall be for the remainder of the term. If the vacancy occurs more than eighteen (18) months prior to the expiration of the term, the appointment shall be until such time as the office is filled by the vote of the qualified electors voting in a special election called by the Council for that purpose, which election shall be held according to the timetable and procedures established by state law generally for the filling of vacancies in elected local offices."?

The members of the council who take office in January 2016 shall cause the nine (9) election districts to be drawn as soon as practicable in order that the Fall 2019 elections utilize such election districts. Section 2-05. Compensation. A. The compensation of council members shall be $12,000 per year for those council members taking office in January 2016 and thereafter, and $20,000 per year for those council members taking office in January 2020 and thereafter, and notwithstanding any contrary provision of the Iberia Parish Home Rule Charter, including, but not limited to, Section 2-05(B), the council may immediately authorize and approve the payments of any additional benefits, such as hospitalization insurance and/or retirement contributions."?

full_text: Shall the Parish of East Feliciana, State of Louisiana (the "Parish"), levy a special tax of two and one-half (2.5) mills on all property subject to taxation in the Parish for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2018 and ending with the year 2027 (an estimated $431,250 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for the purpose of the maintenance, support and operation of a public library, particularly the Audubon Regional Library and its branches?

specific_title: Fire Protection Dist. No. 2 -- 5.63 Mills - BOC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Fire Protection District No. 2 Proposition (Tax Renewal)
full_text: Shall Fire Protection District No. 2 of the Parish of Evangeline, State of Louisiana (the "District"), be authorized to continue to levy a special tax of five and sixty-three hundredths (5.63) mills (the estimated amount reasonably expected to be collected from the levy of the tax for one entire year being $394,663.06), on all the property subject to taxation in the District, the City of Ville Platte excepted, for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2019 and ending with the year 2028, for the purpose of acquiring, constructing, improving, maintaining and operating fire protection facilities in the District, including the purchase of fire trucks and equipment therefor, and the payment of Firemen's salaries?

specific_title: PW Law Enforcement District -- 19 Mills - Sheriff - 20 Yrs.
summary_text: Law Enforcement District Proposition (Millage Renewal)
full_text: Shall the Law Enforcement District of the Parish of Grant, State of Louisiana (the "District"), continue to levy a special tax of nineteen (19) mills on all the property subject to taxation in the District (an estimated $969,400 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for a period of twenty (20) years, beginning with the year 2021 and ending with the year 2040, for the purpose of constructing, improving, maintaining and operating jail facilities for said District?

specific_title: Ward Four Fire Protection Dist. -- $40 Parcel Fee - BOC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Ward Four Fire Protection District Proposition (Parcel Fee Renewal)
full_text: Shall the Ward Four Fire Protection District of the Parish of Jackson, State of Louisiana (the "District") continue to levy, for a period of ten (10) years, beginning the first day of January, 2017, a parcel fee on each parcel of immovable property as defined in Louisiana Revised Statute 40:1505(D) situated within the Ward Four Fire Protection District in the amount of $40.00 per year (an estimated $56,000.00 expected at this time to be collected from the parcel fee for an entire year) to be expended for the purposes of acquiring, constructing, maintaining and operating fire protection and other first response facilities and equipment, including the cost of obtaining water for fire protection purposes and salaries of firemen, and all purposes incidental thereto?

specific_title: Gravity Drainage District No. 7 -- 5.23 Mills - BOC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Gravity Drainage District No. 7 Proposition (Millage Renewal)
full_text: Shall Gravity Drainage District No. 7 of Jefferson Davis Parish, Louisiana (the "District"), be authorized to continue to levy a five and twenty-three hundredths (5.23) mills tax (the estimated amount reasonably expected to be collected from the levy of the tax for one entire year being $64,500) on all property subject for taxation in the District, for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2018 and ending with the year 2027, for the purpose of improving, maintaining and operating gravity drainage works within and for the District?

specific_title: Cons. Gravity Drainage Dist. No. 1 -- 7.75 Mills - BOC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Consolidated Gravity Drainage District No. 1 Proposition (Millage Renewal)
full_text: Shall Consolidated Gravity Drainage District No. 1 of Jefferson Davis Parish, State of Louisiana (the "District"), levy a special tax of seven and seventy-five hundredths (7.75) mills on all property subject to taxation in the District (an estimated $127,400 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2017 and ending with the year 2026, for the purpose of constructing, improving and maintaining gravity drainage works in the District?

specific_title: PW Library Tax Renewal -- 2.91 Mills - PC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Parishwide Proposition (Library Tax Renewal)
full_text: Shall the Parish of Lafayette, State of Louisiana (the "Parish"), continue to levy a special tax of two and ninety-one hundredths (2.91) mills on all property subject to taxation in said Parish (an estimated $6,060,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2017 and ending with the year 2026, for the purpose of the maintenance and support of the public library of Lafayette Parish and its branches?

specific_title: Hospital Service District No. 2 -- 2 Mills - BOC - 10 yrs.
summary_text: Hospital Service District No. 2 Proposition (Tax Renewal)
full_text: Shall Hospital Service District No. 2 of the Parish of Lafourche, State of Louisiana (the "District''), levy a two (2) mills tax on all the property subject to taxation in the District for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2018 and ending with the year 2027 (an estimated $299,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for the purpose of constructing, maintaining and operating the hospital facilities of the District?

specific_title: Village of Simsboro -- 1.25% S&U - Mayor & BOA - Perp.
summary_text: Village of Simsboro Proposition (1.25% Sales Tax)
full_text: Shall the Village of Simsboro, Louisiana (the "Village"), under Article VI, Section 29 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974, and other constitutional and statutory authority, be authorized to levy and collect a tax of one and one-fourth percent (1.25%) (the "Tax"), upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption, and the storage for use or consumption, of tangible personal property and on sales of services in the Village, for a perpetual term commencing January 1, 2017, collections from the Tax for the first year expected to be approximately $2,400, with the proceeds of the Tax (after paying costs of collection and administration), to be dedicated and used for any lawful corporate purpose of the Village, and for authority to fund a portion of the avails of the Tax into Bonds in the manner provided by law?

specific_title: Sewerage District No. 1 -- Merge Sewerage Dist. 1 & 2 - BOC
summary_text: Sewerage District No. 1 Proposition
full_text: In order to consolidate operations, achieve maximum budgetary efficiency and reduce the costs of operations, shall Sewerage District No. 1 of Livingston Parish, Louisiana be granted the authority to merge into Sewerage District No. 2 of Livingston Parish, Louisiana in accordance with Article VI, Section 16 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974, and to take any and all action required to accomplish such merger?

specific_title: Sewerage District No. 2 -- Merge Sewerage Dist. 1 & 2 - BOC
summary_text: Sewerage District No. 2 Proposition
full_text: In order to consolidate operations, achieve maximum budgetary efficiency and reduce the costs of operations, shall Sewerage District No. 1 of Livingston Parish, Louisiana be merged into Sewerage District No. 2 of Livingston Parish, Louisiana in accordance with Article VI, Section 16 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974, and Sewerage District No. 2 of Livingston Parish, Louisiana shall have the authority to take any and all action required to accomplish such merger?

specific_title: Fire Protection Dist. No. 10 -- 8.70 Mills - BOC - 10 Yrs.

specific_title: Fire Protection Dist. No. 1 -- 7.02 Mills - BOC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Fire Protection District No. 1 Proposition (Millage Renewal)
full_text: Shall Fire Protection District No. 1 of the Parish of Natchitoches, State of Louisiana (the "District"), continue to levy and collect a special tax of seven and two hundredths (7.02) mills on all property subject to taxation within the District (an estimated $226,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2017 and ending with the year 2026, for the purpose of acquiring, constructing, improving, maintaining and/or operating fire protection facilities and equipment in the District, including paying the cost of obtaining water for fire protection purposes?

specific_title: School District No. 9 -- $18M Bond - SB - 20 Yrs.
summary_text: School District No. 9 Proposition (Bond)
full_text: Shall School District No. 9 of Natchitoches Parish, Louisiana (the "District"), incur debt and issue bonds to the amount of not exceeding Eighteen Million Dollars ($18,000,000), in one or more series, to run not exceeding twenty (20) years from date thereof, with interest at a rate or rates not exceeding six per centum (6%) per annum, for the purpose of acquiring and/or improving lands for building sites and playgrounds, including construction of necessary sidewalks and streets adjacent thereto; purchasing, erecting and/or improving school buildings and other school related facilities within and for the District and acquiring the necessary equipment and furnishings therefor, title to which shall be in the public; which bonds will be general obligations of the District and will be payable from ad valorem taxes to be levied and collected in the manner provided by Article VI, Section 33 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974 and statutory authority supplemental thereto, with an estimated 7 mills to be levied in the first year of issue to pay said Bonds?

specific_title: Sales Tax District No. 1 -- 1/2% S&U Tax - PC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Sales Tax District No. 1 Proposition (City and Parish Roads Sales Tax)
full_text: Shall Sales Tax District No. 1 of the Parish of Natchitoches, State of Louisiana (the "District") whose boundaries are the Parish of Natchitoches excluding the area within the Town of Campti, be authorized to levy and collect for a period of ten (10) years from and after April 1, 2017, a tax of one-half percent (1/2%) (the "Tax") upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption, and the storage for use or consumption, of tangible personal property and on sales of services within the District as defined by law, (an estimated $3,250,000 expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the Tax for an entire year), with the proceeds thereof (after paying the expenses of collecting and administering the Tax), to be dedicated for construction, improving and maintaining public infrastructure within the District with one-half of such Tax revenues collected within the City of Natchitoches being expended for the construction, improving and maintaining of roads, bridges and drainage systems within the City of Natchitoches and the remainder of the proceeds of the Tax being expended for the construction, improving and maintaining of roads and bridges in the remainder of the District?

specific_title: Sales Tax District No. 2 -- .75% S&U Tax - PC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Sales Tax District No. 2 Proposition (Parish Roads Sales Tax)
full_text: Shall Sales Tax District No. 2 of the Parish of Natchitoches, State of Louisiana (the "District") whose boundaries are the Parish of Natchitoches excluding the areas within the City of Natchitoches and the Town of Campti, be authorized to levy and collect for a period of ten (10) years from and after April 1, 2017, a tax of three-quarter of one percent (.75%) (the "Tax") upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption, and the storage for use or consumption, of tangible personal property and on sales of services within the District as defined by law, (an estimated $1,500,000 expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the Tax for an entire year), with the proceeds thereof (after paying the expenses of collecting and administering the Tax), to be dedicated for constructing, improving and maintaining public roads and bridges in the District?

summary_text: Parishwide Proposition (City Charter Amendment - Financial and Operational Independence of the Office of Inspector General, Office of Independent Police Monitor, and Ethics Review Board)
full_text: Shall Sections 9-401 and 9-402 of the Home Rule Charter of the City of New Orleans be amended and new Sections 9-403, 9-404 and 9-405 be enacted relative to the financial and operational independence of the Office of lnspector General, Office of lndependent Police Monitor, and Ethics Review Board, effective January 1, 2017: (1) to apportion funding among the three local ethics entities; (2) to establish each such local ethics entity as financially and operationally independent; and (3) to provide for annual independent external evaluation procedures for each such entity?

specific_title: Oak Island Neighborhood Improvement Dist. -- $150 Parcel Fee - CC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Oak Island Neighborhood Improvement District Proposition
full_text: Shall the City of New Orleans impose and collect a special annual fee, called the Oak Island Neighborhood Improvement District fee, on each improved parcel of land in the Oak Island Neighborhood Improvement District (Michoud Blvd., from Adventure Dr. to Expedition Dr. (both sides), to Explorer Ave., to Voyageur Dr. and Voyageur Ct. (both sides), to Horizon Dr. (both sides) to Pierre Ct. (both sides); also Michoud Blvd.; to W. Cavelier Dr. (both sides), to Trapper Ct. (both sides), to St. Marie Ct. (both sides) and N. Cavelier Dr. (both sides)), except parcels whose owner(s) qualified for the special assessment level provided by Louisiana Constitution Article VII, Section 18(G)(1), in the amount of and not exceeding one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00), for ten (10) years beginning January 1, 2017 and ending December 31, 2026, which fee is estimated to generate approximately $45,000.00 annually, to be used solely and exclusively to promote and encourage the security, beautification and overall betterment of Oak Island Neighborhood Improvement District, except a 1% City collection fee, which additional security and services shall be supplemental to and not in lieu of personnel and services provided in the district by the state, city, or other political subdivisions?

specific_title: Lake Forest Estates Improvement Dist. -- $485 Parcel Fee - CC - 8 Yrs.
summary_text: Lake Forest Estates Improvement District Proposition
full_text: Shall the City of New Orleans levy a special annual fee, to be called the Lake Forest Estates Improvement District's fee, on each parcel of taxable real property situated within the boundaries of the Lake Forest Estates Improvement District (which District is comprised of that area of the Parish of Orleans whose boundaries are coterminous with the boundaries of the Lake Forest Estates) as specified by Resolution R-16-122 of the City Council of New Orleans in the amount of Four Hundred Eighty-Five dollars ($485) annually for eight (8) years, beginning January 1, 2019 and ending December 31, 2026, with an estimated $95,338.00 expected annually to be collected from the levy of the parcel fee for an entire year, to be used solely and exclusively for the primary object and purpose of promoting and encouraging the beautification, security and overall betterment of the District, except a 1% City collection fee, as determined and managed by the Board of Directors of the Lake Forest Estates Improvement District which security shall be supplemental to and not in lieu of personnel and services provided in the District by the New Orleans Police Department?

specific_title: Lake Vista Crime Prevention Dist. -- $220 Parcel Fee - CC - 4 Yrs.
summary_text: Lake Vista Crime Prevention District Proposition
full_text: Shall the City of New Orleans renew the special annual "Lake Vista Crime Prevention District Parcel Fee," on each improved or unimproved single- and two-family residential parcel and each multiple-dwelling or apartment parcel located within the Lake Vista Crime Prevention District (which district is located within and including the following perimeter: Robert E. Lee Boulevard (interior side), Marconi Drive (interior side), Beauregard Avenue (interior side), and Lakeshore Drive (interior side)), in the amount of not to exceed two hundred twenty dollars ($220) per parcel annually for four (4) years starting January 1, 2017 and ending December 31, 2020, which fee is estimated to generate approximately one hundred sixty-five thousand dollars ($165,000) annually, to be used solely and exclusively to promote and encourage the security of the Lake Vista Crime Prevention District as determined and managed by the Board of Commissioners of the Lake Vista Crime Prevention District, which additional security patrols (public or private) or any other security or other services or betterments provided by the district shall be supplemental to and not in lieu of personnel and services provided in the district by the City, State or by other political subdivisions?

specific_title: Lakeshore Crime Prevention Dist. -- $360 Parcel Fee - CC - 4 Yrs.
summary_text: Lakeshore Crime Prevention District Proposition
full_text: Shall the City of New Orleans levy and collect the Lakeshore Crime Prevention District parcel fee on each improved or unimproved parcel located within the Lakeshore Crime Prevention District (the "District") in the amount of and not exceeding three hundred sixty dollars ($360.00) annually, for four (4) years beginning January 1, 2017 and ending December 31, 2020, which fee is estimated to generate approximately $236,520 annually, to be used solely and exclusively to promote and encourage security in the Lakeshore Crime Prevention District, except a 1% City collection fee, which additional security and services shall be supplemental to and not in lieu of personnel and services provided in the District by the New Orleans Police Department?

specific_title: Monroe Special School Dist. Prop. No. 1 -- 14.41 Mills - SB - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: City of Monroe Special School District Propositions Proposition No. 1 (Millage Renewal)
full_text: Shall the City of Monroe Special School District (through the Monroe City School Board, acting as the governing authority thereof), as a special school district acting under the authority of Article VIII, Section 10 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, and other constitutional and statutory authority, be authorized to continue to levy and collect a tax of fourteen and forty-one hundredths (14.41) mills on all the property subject to taxation in said school district (an estimated $5,200,000.00 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year) for a period of ten (10) years, commencing with the year 2017 and ending with the year 2026, for the purpose of maintaining and operating the city schools of the Monroe City School Board?

specific_title: Monroe Special School Dist. Prop. No. 2 -- 6.15 Mills - SB - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: City of Monroe Special School District Propositions Proposition No. 2 (Millage Continuation)
full_text: Shall the City of Monroe Special School District (through the Monroe City School Board, acting as the governing authority thereof), as a special school district acting under the authority of Article VIII, Section 10 of the Louisiana Constitution of 1974, and other constitutional and statutory authority, be authorized to continue to levy and collect a tax of six and fifteen hundredths (6.15) mills on all the property subject to taxation in said school district, said mills to represent a 0.01 mills increase over the 6.14 mills authorized to be levied through the year 2016 pursuant to an election held on April 29, 2006 (an estimated $2,200,000.00 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year) for a period of ten (10) years, commencing with the year 2017 and ending with the year 2026, for the purpose of giving and providing additional aid and support to the city schools of the Monroe City School Board, provided proceeds from said tax will not be used for payment of salaries of professional personnel?

specific_title: PW Prop. (Sales Tax Renewal) -- 1/4% S&U Tax - PJ - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Parishwide Proposition (Sales Tax Renewal)
full_text: Shall the Parish of Pointe Coupee, State of Louisiana (the "Parish"), under the provisions of Article VI, Section 29 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974 and Section 338.54 of Title 47 of the Louisiana Revised Statutes of 1950, as amended, and other constitutional and statutory authority supplemental thereto, be authorized to continue to levy and collect a tax of one-fourth of one percent (1/4%) (the "Tax") upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption and storage for use or consumption of tangible personal property and on the sales of services in the Parish, all as defined by law, (an estimated $850,665 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the Tax for an entire year), for a period of 10 years, from July 1, 2017, the proceeds of the Tax (after paying reasonable and necessary costs and expenses of collecting and administering the Tax), to be dedicated to and used solely for capital improvements, maintenance and operation of the Pointe Coupee Parish Health Services District Number One?

specific_title: PW HRC Plan of Government -- Adopt HRC - PJ
summary_text: Parishwide Proposition
full_text: Shall the Home Rule Charter Plan of Government for Pointe Coupee Parish prepared and submitted by the duly constituted Home Rule Charter Commission according to Article VI, Section 5 of the Constitution of Louisiana, and other applicable law, be adopted?

specific_title: Road Dist. No. 1 Prop. No. 1 -- 8 Mills - PJ - 10 Yrs.

full_text: Shall Road District No. 1 of St. Helena Parish, Louisiana (the "District"), be authorized to levy a special tax of eight (8) mills on all property subject to taxation within the District (an estimated $128,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2020 and ending with the year 2029, for the purpose of constructing, improving, maintaining and keeping in repair the public roads, highways and bridges in the District?

specific_title: Road Lighting Dist. No. 2 -- 3.99 Mills - PC - 10 Yrs.

Lee Boulevard, Pratt Drive, St. Bernard Avenue, the shoreline of Lake Pontchartrain, and Lakeshore Drive, as specified by New Orleans City Council, for a period of eight (8) years, commencing January 1, 2019 and ending December 31, 2026, which fee is estimated to generate approximately $130,500 annually, to be used solely and exclusively for the prevention of crime and the provision of additional security by providing an increase of the presence of law enforcement officers and/or duly authorized security personnel within the District as determined and managed by the Board of Commissioners of the District, which law enforcement officers and/or additional security patrols are paid using funds from the proceeds of the Parcel Fee and that any additional law enforcement officers and/or security patrols are supplemental to and not in lieu of personnel and services provided by the New Orleans Police Department?

full_text: In lieu of 3.00 mills currently levied for Parkway and Parks Commission and New Orleans Recreation Department and 0.32 mills and 2.99 mills levied for Audubon Commission ("Prior Taxes"), shall the City be authorized to levy a special tax of 6.31 mills ("Tax") for twenty years, January 1, 2021 - December 31, 2040 (estimated at $22,150,000 in the first year) with proceeds dedicated first to payment of debt service obligations secured by the Prior Taxes then to improving park safety and accessibility, capturing stormwater to reduce flooding, repairing and upgrading playgrounds and recreation centers, conserving natural areas, and constructing, improving, maintaining, and operating parks, recreational, and wildlife conservation facilities in the City, except that a portion of collections shall be remitted to certain state and statewide retirement systems as required by law, allocated pro-rata as follows: 1.95 mills to New Orleans Recreation Development Commission; 1.80 mills to New Orleans Department of Parks and Parkways; 0.61 mills to City Park Improvement Association; and 1.95 mills to Audubon Commission, supplemental to and not in lieu of City general fund appropriations budgeted for 2020, subject to requirements provided by Ordinance Calendar Number 32,501 and with expenditures subject to public disclosure through annual audits?

full_text: Shall Gravity Drainage District Number Five (5), Assumption Parish, Louisiana (the "District"), continue to impose, levy and collect annually for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2021 and ending with the year 2030, an acreage tax, or forced contribution, not to exceed thirty-five cents ($.35) per acre (an estimated $623 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), on every acre of land in said District for the purpose of maintaining, improving and keeping in repair the system of gravity drainage constructed in said District?

specific_title: PW School District -- 10 Mills Renewal - SB - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Parishwide School District Proposition (Millage Renewal)
full_text: Shall Parishwide School District of the Parish of Avoyelles, State of Louisiana (the "District"), levy and collect a special tax of ten (10) mills on all of the property subject to taxation in said District (an estimated $1,520,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2022 and ending with the year 2031, for the payment of salaries and benefits for the employees of the Parish School Board, provided that the District shall not be authorized to levy and collect the Tax unless the proposed Avoyelles School Board sales tax on this ballot is also approved by the electorate?

specific_title: PW School Board -- 1/4% S&U Tax Renewal - SB - 10 Yrs.

full_text: Shall the Parish School Board of the Parish of Avoyelles, State of Louisiana (the "Parish"), under the provisions of Article VI, Section 29 of the Constitution of the State of Louisiana of 1974, and other constitutional and statutory authority, be authorized to levy and collect a tax of one-fourth percent (1/4%) (the "Tax") (an estimated $1,000,000 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the Tax for an entire year) upon the sale at retail, the use, the lease or rental, the consumption, and the storage for use or consumption, of tangible personal property and on sales of services in the Parish, all as defined by law, for a period of ten (10) years, commencing January 1, 2022, with the proceeds thereof (after paying the reasonable and necessary expenses of collecting and administering the Tax), to be dedicated for the payment of salaries and benefits for the employees of the Parish School Board, provided that the School Board shall not be authorized to levy and collect the Tax unless the proposed Avoyelles Parishwide School District millage on this ballot is also approved by the electorate?

specific_title: Parishwide Proposition (Health Unit/Public Health) -- 2.42 Mills Continuation - PJ - 10 Yrs.

full_text: Shall the Parish of Beauregard, State of Louisiana (the "Parish"), be authorized to levy a special tax of two and forty-two hundredths (2.42) mills (the "Tax") (the estimated amount reasonably expected to be collected from the levy of the tax for one entire year being $670,000) on all the property subject to taxation within the Parish for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2021 and ending with the year 2030, with the proceeds of the Tax to be dedicated and used to acquire, construct, improve, maintain and/or operate the public health units and other related public health activities in the Parish, said millage to represent an eighteen hundredths of a mill (.18) increase over the 2.24 mills tax authorized to be levied through the year 2020 pursuant to an election held on October 17, 2009?

specific_title: Fire Protection District No. 6 -- 7 Mills - BOC - 10 Yrs.

full_text: Shall Bienville Parish Fire Protection District No. 6, State of Louisiana (the "District"), levy a seven (7) mills tax on all property subject to taxation in the District (an estimated $443,500 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2021 and ending with the year 2030, for the purpose of acquiring, constructing, improving, maintaining, operating and/or purchasing fire protection equipment and facilities and emergency medical service facilities, vehicles and equipment for the District, including payment of salaries in connection therewith?

specific_title: Parishwide Proposition -- 3.02 Mills Continuation - PJ - 10 Yrs.

specific_title: Village of Grayson -- 1% S&U Tax - VC - 10 Yrs.
summary_text: Village of Grayson Proposition (Sales Tax)
full_text: Shall the Village of Grayson of the Parish of Caldwell, State of Louisiana (the "Village"), under the provisions of Article VI, Section 29 of the 1974 Louisiana Constitution, and other constitutional and statutory authority, be authorized to levy and collect a tax of one percent (1%) ("Tax"), with annual Tax collections estimated to be $23,334.33, upon sale at retail, use, lease or rental, consumption and storage for use or consumption of tangible personal property, and sale of services within the Village, for a period of ten (10) years beginning April 1, 2021, with Tax proceeds dedicated to funding maintenance and operation of publicly owned infrastructure improvements and for economic development purposes of the Village?

specific_title: Parishwide Proposition No. 1 of 3 -- 2.18 Mills Renewal - PJ - 10 Yrs.

full_text: Shall the Parish of Caldwell, State of Louisiana (the "Parish"), continue to levy a two and eighteen hundredths (2.18) mills tax on all the property subject to taxation in the Parish (an estimated $140,610 reasonably expected at this time to be collected from the levy of the tax for an entire year), for a period of ten (10) years, beginning with the year 2021 and ending with the year 2030, for the purpose of (i) funding a reserve of $50,000 for industrial operations and maintenance and job inducement at the Caldwell Parish Industrial Park and (ii) the remainder of the proceeds of the Tax to be used for the purpose of improving, maintaining and operating the 911 emergency telephone system in the Parish, including the acquisition and maintenance of the necessary facilities and equipment therefor?

specific_title: Parishwide Proposition No. 2 of 3 -- 3.29 Mills Renewal - PJ - 10 Yrs.

specific_title: Parishwide Proposition No. 3 of 3 -- 7.13 Mills Renewal - PJ - 10 Yrs.
